knowledges.content: Under joint Agentic RL optimization, reasoning and tool-use capabilities exhibit a seesaw phenomenon: improving one consistently degrades the other. This is observed across Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-7B, and Llama3.1-8B, and persists at multiple training checkpoints.
knowledges.label: seesaw_phenomenon

metadata.prior_justification: Observed across 4 model families (Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-7B, Llama3.1-8B) at multiple checkpoints. Joint training degrades both capabilities vs single-capability training. -0.05: 7-8B only; -0.03: single RL framework (veRL).

knowledges.title: Seesaw phenomenon: reasoning-tool-use trade-off in ARL

knowledges.content: The seesaw phenomenon is caused by gradient-level conflict between reasoning and tool-use capabilities, not by data imbalance. Evidence: (1) adjusting the data mixture ratio fails to resolve interference, (2) LEAS gradient analysis shows consistently negative interaction coefficients λ23 (mean ≈ -0.3 across checkpoints), (3) the interaction component dominates over capability-isolation components when they interfere.
knowledges.label: gradient_conflict_is_root_cause

metadata.prior_justification: Three convergent lines: (1) data mixture sweep fails, (2) LEAS lambda23 < 0 across checkpoints, (3) interaction component dominates. -0.08: LEAS is linear approximation; -0.07: no intervention experiment.

knowledges.title: Gradient conflict is the root cause of capability interference

knowledges.content: DART (Disentangled Agentic RL Tuning) resolves the gradient conflict by applying hard token-level routing through separate LoRA adapters with frozen backbone. It achieves: (1) +4.91 on Qwen3-8B MATH with tool-use intact, (2) consistent improvement across three backbones and two model sizes, (3) robustness to LoRA rank choice, (4) simpler infrastructure than 2-agent alternatives. The key mechanism is structural gradient isolation — DART guarantees zero interaction term between the two capabilities' gradients.
knowledges.label: dart_solves_gradient_conflict

metadata.prior_justification: Structural zero-interaction guarantee + consistent +3.15 to +4.91 across 3 backbones + rank insensitivity. -0.07: no Llama; -0.05: max 7B.

knowledges.title: DART structurally eliminates gradient conflict between capabilities

knowledges.content: DART outperforms or matches all tested alternatives: (1) standard GRPO (+6.35% avg EM across benchmarks), (2) task-specific LoRA (which cannot disentangle interference), (3) 2-agent systems (DART approaches their performance while using ~1/8 memory and simpler infrastructure). The 2-agent comparison is the closest — DART is within 1.2pp on most benchmarks.
knowledges.label: dart_vs_alternatives

metadata.prior_justification: Beats GRPO (+6.35%) and task-LoRA, approaches 2-agent (~1.2pp). -0.10: 1.2pp may be within benchmark variance; -0.10: no GPT-4o; -0.05: Qwen-only.

knowledges.title: DART vs alternatives: better or comparable with simpler infrastructure

knowledges.content: LEAS (Linear Effect Attribution System) provides a quantitative framework for measuring capability-level interference in ARL. It decomposes the model's output into reasoning-isolated, tool-use-isolated, and interaction components via logit-level linear attribution, enabling per-checkpoint tracking of how capabilities evolve and interfere during training.
knowledges.label: leas_diagnostic_framework

metadata.prior_justification: Identifiability satisfied when design matrix invertible. -0.10: linearity; -0.08: logit-level may not represent decoded behavior.

knowledges.title: LEAS quantitatively measures capability-level interference

knowledges.content: Agentic RL (ARL) trains LLMs to interleave reasoning with tool calls (search, code execution) under a single RL objective over shared parameters. Prior work (Toolformer, Search-R1, DeepSeekMath) applies one RL update per complete trajectory.
knowledges.label: arl_training_setup
knowledges.title: ARL training paradigm

knowledges.content: No experimental validation on Llama-series models or models > 7B. All main experiments use Qwen-series 7-8B. This limits confidence in cross-architecture generalization.
knowledges.label: no_llama_validation

metadata.prior_justification: Documented limitation, not a contested claim.

knowledges.title: Limitation: no Llama or >7B validation

knowledges.content: Experiments are limited to single-turn agent tasks. Multi-turn interactions may introduce additional interference patterns not captured by the current LEAS framework.
knowledges.label: single_turn_scope

metadata.prior_justification: Single-turn agent tasks only; multi-turn may add interference.

knowledges.title: Limitation: single-turn scope

knowledges.content: Adjusting the reasoning vs tool-use data mixture ratio fails to eliminate capability interference. λ23 stays negative across mixture sweeps, indicating a gradient-level rather than data-level source.
knowledges.label: surprise_data_mix_useless

metadata.prior_justification: Direct experimental observation: lambda23 stays negative across data-mix sweeps.

knowledges.title: Surprising: data mixture tuning is ineffective

knowledges.content: DART's improvement is robust to LoRA rank choice. Performance is nearly flat across a wide rank sweep, indicating the routing mechanism (not adapter capacity) drives the gain.
knowledges.label: surprise_dart_rank_insensitive

metadata.prior_justification: Direct ablation reading from Fig 5 — performance flat across rank values.

knowledges.title: Surprising: DART improvement is rank-insensitive

knowledges.content: Reported negative result: sweeping data-mixture ratios within ARL training does not eliminate the seesaw pattern. Excludes data imbalance as the dominant cause.
knowledges.label: neg_data_mix_fails

metadata.prior_justification: Reported negative result from ablation experiments.

knowledges.title: Negative result: data mixture sweep fails to remove seesaw

knowledges.content: Reported negative result: task-level LoRA switching performs comparably to vanilla SearchR1. Modular adapters alone are insufficient; token-level routing is required.
knowledges.label: neg_task_lora_fails

metadata.prior_justification: Reported in ablation: task-level LoRA ≈ vanilla SearchR1.

knowledges.title: Negative result: task-level LoRA does not disentangle

knowledges.content: Reported negative result: hybrid models built by composing reasoning-isolated and tool-use-isolated subnetworks at inference underperform the linear-decomposition prediction.
knowledges.label: neg_inference_hybrid_fails

metadata.prior_justification: Reported in Table 3: hybrid composition does not match linear-decomposition prediction.

knowledges.title: Negative result: inference-time hybrid is not replicable

knowledges.content: DART's gap to the 2-agent baseline is only ~1.2pp — within typical LLM benchmark variance. Without multi-seed CI the equivalence claim is not statistically established.
knowledges.label: weak_dart_vs_2agent_marginal

metadata.prior_justification: The 1.2pp gap is a fact; whether within statistical noise is the open question (no CI reported).
metadata.what_would_falsify: multi-seed (>=5) reruns with 95% CI; CI straddling 0 falsifies equivalence

knowledges.title: Weak premise: DART vs 2-agent equivalence not statistically established

knowledges.content: No intervention experiment verifying gradient conflict causes seesaw. Evidence is correlational.
knowledges.label: weak_correlation_not_causation

metadata.prior_justification: Methodological fact: paper does not run an intervention experiment.
metadata.what_would_falsify: inject synthetic gradient conflict; project away to see seesaw vanish

knowledges.title: Weak premise: no causal intervention, only correlation

knowledges.content: LEAS decomposition is defined at the logit level with linear identifiability. Non-linear interactions below the logit layer may remain invisible.
knowledges.label: weak_leas_logit_only

metadata.prior_justification: LEAS construction is explicitly logit-level and linear by definition.
metadata.what_would_falsify: behavioural A/B on λ23≈0 checkpoints showing residual interference

knowledges.title: Weak premise: LEAS limited to linear logit-level decomposition

knowledges.content: All main DART experiments use Qwen-series 7-8B models. Llama, Mistral, and >8B scales are untested.
knowledges.label: bdry_qwen_only

metadata.prior_justification: Direct fact: experiments table lists only Qwen-series 7-8B.

knowledges.title: Boundary premise: Qwen 7-8B scope

knowledges.content: DART's zero-interaction guarantee is derived under the LoRA+frozen backbone setup; full-parameter fine-tuning is not covered.
knowledges.label: bdry_lora_only

metadata.prior_justification: Direct mathematical fact: zero-interaction theorem is stated for the LoRA path with frozen backbone.

knowledges.title: Boundary premise: LoRA + frozen backbone only

knowledges.content: DART unifies four ad-hoc techniques with a single structural change: token-level hard routing plus frozen backbone, yielding a provable zero-interaction property.
knowledges.label: elegant_dart_token_routing

metadata.prior_justification: Methodological quality assessment; prior reflects clear structural proof plus empirical confirmation.

knowledges.title: Elegant: DART's token-level routing unifies prior ad-hoc methods

knowledges.content: LEAS decomposes multi-capability logits into capability + interaction components via six contrast models and a linear identifiability condition — compact and non-invasive to training.
knowledges.label: elegant_leas_decomposition

metadata.prior_justification: Linear-decomposition method is well-defined; prior reflects identifiability condition being explicit and verifiable.

knowledges.title: Elegant: LEAS's 6-contrast linear decomposition

module_titles.motivation: Layer 2 semantic claims — aggregated from Layer 1 96 claims.

metadata.reason: Seesaw exists and data-mixture sweep fails to remove it. Together these narrow the mechanism to gradient-level interference.
Direct positive evidence for a non-data mechanism.

If (a) gradient conflict is the root cause, (b) LEAS provides a valid measurement framework, (c) task-level LoRA alone fails, (d) post-hoc composition fails, (e) DART is rank-insensitive, AND the claim is scoped to (f) LoRA+frozen-backbone and (g) Qwen 7-8B — then DART structurally resolves the interference within its stated scope. If empirical contradictions appear (e.g., Llama failures), BP will assign penalty to the relevant premises.

If DART structurally resolves the interference, its efficiency and performance edge over alternatives follows — but the 2-agent equivalence claim depends on the statistical significance premise. If future multi-seed evidence shows the 1.2pp gap is real, BP penalises weak_dart_vs_2agent_marginal.
